public_rationale: Marcus predicted that once the numbers are fully out, Anthropic will prove more efficient than OpenAI. He set no deadline. The trigger is full disclosure from both companies. Anthropic's S-1 went public on 26 October 2026, showing about $16.3 billion of first-half 2026 revenue against $2.4 billion cost of revenue. OpenAI has only filed a confidential draft. An EDGAR check on 13 October 2026 found no public OpenAI prospectus, and I found no later filing. The like-for-like comparison he described is not yet possible, so the forecast is open.
limitations: The EDGAR status comes from a secondary tracker, because OpenAI's own announcement page could not be read.
Even after both filings are public, efficiency could be measured in several ways, and revenue-recognition differences complicate comparison.

conditions: when the numbers are fully out

statement.excerpt: I think you will [see] when the numbers are really fully out, then anthropic is more efficient.
statement.document_title: Breaking news, and how the end might begin

from_speaker: when the numbers are really fully out
our_interpretation: Plain reading: once both Anthropic's and OpenAI's full financials are public (for example, public S-1 prospectuses with audited statements), Anthropic will show better efficiency. That means more revenue per dollar of compute and total cost, or a smaller cash burn relative to revenue.
The trigger is that both companies' numbers are fully out. One company's prospectus alone does not allow the comparison.
criteria.support_condition: Public, audited financials for both companies show that Anthropic turns compute and operating spending into revenue more efficiently than OpenAI, for example through a higher gross margin and lower losses or burn relative to revenue on a comparable basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Public, audited financials for both companies show that OpenAI is as efficient as Anthropic or more efficient on those measures.

evidence.locator: section 'What is confirmed about the OpenAI IPO?', paragraph 2
evidence.explanation: OpenAI's financials were still not public in mid-October 2026, so the 'numbers fully out' trigger had not happened for both companies.

evidence.excerpt: Anthropic reported its cost of revenue as $2.38 billion as of June 30, 2026, booking $16.29 billion in revenue during the same period and implying a gross margin of 85%.
evidence.locator: live update 'Anthropic's implied gross margins have exploded', Oct 26 12:12 PM

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A public OpenAI S-1 or other audited financials, compared with Anthropic's S-1 on gross margin, operating loss and cash burn relative to revenue on a consistent revenue basis.
